text.content:
Card conventions

These conventions apply to the current catalog.

Learn, declare, resolve

Tier diamonds show minimum level 1, 3 or 7, with Novice purchases allowed during level-0 creation. Standard DP costs are 2, 4 and 8. All printed discipline ranks must be owned before purchase. No lower-tier ability is required unless Bruce explicitly approves an exception; the current design uses no chains. Signature cards require only the class and level. Ordinary items and ancestry traits are not DP abilities.

The six 1-DP shared Novice exceptions are @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.7dde82adde18027d.JournalEntryPage.b2ef1858c60e2bb9]{Another Tongue}, @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.b4565a3b337dbeff.JournalEntryPage.7c9f1a253b6cb770]{Message by Heart}, @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.f5652824162887a4.JournalEntryPage.d8a671e34b09d015]{Catch That!}, @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.5adbcc730f2a96d9.JournalEntryPage.280d142f0dec2a6b]{A Party Piece}, @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.f9dbc60f1099db35.JournalEntryPage.415ad91e3af6e6c1]{Quick Exit}, @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.df88475aa1da8afe.JournalEntryPage.c77bfa5af0bcbb7e]{Look Over Here!}. Each requires no discipline, may be purchased during level-0 creation or later, and may be purchased only once. They are paid abilities, not free Universal cards. The printed price applies; their tier remains 1.

Declare a card before rolling. Roll 3d6 plus its one printed attribute with the normal Boon/Bane rules. No skill bonus, weapon damage die or extra attribute damage. A no-roll card simply does what it says. Rolled cards give their Weak, Standard and Strong results in the text; a shared 1/2/3 progression always follows that order.

Range uses squares. “Adjacent” means within one square with an actual accessible path. Visible targets still require an attack path. A player area/multitarget attack uses one roll with the worst applicable net Boon/Bane situation. NPC attacks give each affected player a defense roll. A printed NPC defense attribute is a choice for that attack, not the attribute a player attacker rolls.

Costs and time

Main Action, Maneuver, Reaction, Movement and Passive are distinct labels. A long activity prints its full time; “Main Action” does not allow an hour of treatment in one turn. No-roll does not mean free. A triggered Passive effect spends no action unless stated. A Reaction spends the one available Reaction.

Instant damage or displacement occurs once. A named temporary condition continues under the condition rules, not forever because the attack’s duration is Instant. “Once per turn” means your turn unless a different creature’s turn is named. “Once per round” resets at the start of your next turn. “Scene” means one continuous situation; a brief pause does not reset it.

Healing costs 1/3/7 HP by tier, paid before the roll, bypassing resistance and leaving the caster above 0. Requires a free hand. Healing resistance is Life resistance; minimum 1 applies only when HP is missing. No healing above maximum. Potions use their own fixed value and inventory die, with no spell outcome roll or caster cost.

Equipment and grants

A grant supplies a missing ordinary item on acquisition. It does not supply another compatible weapon just because another attack was learned, and selling the item does not reactivate a past grant. Ordinary melee and ranged weapons each use Bulk 1. Their names and appearance add no damage. Special equipment adds only printed effects. A requirement without a grant may require treasure or coins; flag that in starter advice.

Bonus and effect language

Same-kind numeric bonuses use the highest. Boons/Banes stack normally. Numbered conditions stack where meaningful; repeated binary Prone does not become Prone 2. Free attacks never trigger more free attacks. A free attack does not consume actions, but only the granting effect determines what attack is permitted.

Displacements use the shared movement rules. “Move without provoking” does not allow walking through walls or occupied standing creatures. Teleportation is explicit. Flavor never silently grants flight, telepathy, armor, a second damage type or immunity.

Proposed sorting types

Attack, Defense, Movement, Control, Recovery, Utility, Skill, Magic, Crafting, Training and Signature are tags, not additional rules. Multiple tags are allowed. Action cost is indexed separately. Ancestry, Origin, Discipline, Equipment and Recipe identify record kinds rather than learned-card prerequisites.

Printed layout later: numbered diamond top left, name top center, discipline icons top right. Type, action, range, outcomes, duration and limits remain visible. Color can support the tier but may never replace its number.

A different kind of expertise

The attribute printed on the chosen card is the one you roll. Anatomy of an Opening makes Knowledge a way to fight; Smile Before Steel uses Guile; The Untroubled Hand uses Reason. They are distinct techniques, not permission to replace every attack’s attribute. When a card explicitly replaces a defense attribute, declare and pay its Reaction before rolling. No extra modifier is added.

Beast forms keep your own HP, wounds and attributes; they are not disposable HP pools. Use the form’s printed actions and equipment restrictions. The new cards state how to enter and leave a form, so the table does not need a monster stat block.

Noncombat cards should be read as things a person can do. Correct ordinary action still needs no roll when no consequence is at stake. An expert adds an opportunity, useful detail or reliability; owning the card is not a license for everyone else to stop thinking creatively.

Imagine it, then resolve it

Agreed October 13, 2026. Every card begins with narrative text describing what using it looks, sounds or feels like. One vivid sentence is enough for a simple ability; a more elaborate ability may deserve more. Address the player and make an action or experience imaginable. This applies to universal actions, signatures, shared abilities and the other character, equipment and recipe records.

Follow the narrative with a distinct Rules section. Only this section establishes mechanical permissions and effects. State who acts, the target, action or full time, attribute or no-roll instruction, prerequisites, costs, outcomes, duration and limits as applicable. A triggered effect states its trigger and resolution timing. A movement effect states its distance and legal endpoints. A benefit states its recipients and expiry. Do not bury any of these in the narrative.

For example, “You tie the knot without looking, then test it with a tug” evokes experience. “While climbing, secure one held rope at a reachable suitable anchor without a separate action; a free hand is required” is the adjudicated rule. Narrative does not imply an extra sense, free item, automatic success or magical power.

Keep acquisition facts in Rules too. An origin’s memory prompt belongs above Rules; its paired discipline/card grant belongs below. For an item, describe the experience of handling it, then specify its actual additive effects and use requirements.

Development breadth

Agreed direction October 13, 2026: aim for approximately 10–15 shared Passive abilities, including useful enduring expertise outside combat. This count excludes ancestry traits and class-exclusive signatures; it is a design target, not a rule limiting what a character may learn. Including the small 1-DP options, the shared catalog has eighteen.

Higher-tier utility should change the problems a character can tackle or the people they can help, rather than merely repeat ordinary 1/2/3 progress. Use mixed discipline requirements when both fields contribute to the technique. “A 2 and B 1” requires both ranks before learning; it does not require an earlier ability. Preserve strong single-discipline rank-3 destinations and class-and-level-only signature requirements.

Named abilities use their printed requirements.

Bruce also accepts the revised grant-only menu of up to 35 eligible unowned shared choices as useful breadth. Evaluate their distinctness and value rather than adding prerequisites solely to reduce the count.

Concrete language review

Bruce’s correction, October 13, 2026: a narrative heading and an evocative slogan are insufficient. Describe what the character actually does and what becomes visible, audible or felt. “You reach for tomorrow’s sky” leaves the action unspecified. Reaching through a tear in the air, pulling out a clump of weather and tossing it onto the ground gives the player an action to imagine. Passive expertise may instead describe the practiced habit or observation that produces its benefit.

Read the narrative independently of the title and rules. Could a player describe that action to the table? Does it suggest the effect this card actually supplies? Avoid replacing a specific action with a promise, maxim or mysterious metaphor. Sensory detail should make the action clearer; it should not imply an extra power.

Read the rules in the order someone uses them: choose the target, meet requirements, pay the action/cost, make any roll, apply the result, then track its expiry. Explain unusual dice operations on the card. “Lowest retained die” is not sufficient: say which dice are examined after Boons/Banes and whether the printed numbers or modified total matter. Put separate effects in separate sentences or bullets. Show Weak, Standard and Strong rather than compressing a whole procedure into unexplained slashes.

Finally, read every field against the card’s purpose. A swimming card must not carry a wound-treatment limit; an area card should say which creatures it affects rather than recite rules for unrelated target shapes. Structural checks cannot perform this editorial review, and passing them must not be presented as proof that wording is clear.

Table and VTT resolution

Review revision, October 13, 2026. Read a card in this order: check permission and equipment, declare choices and targets, pay its action and costs, roll if called for, apply the complete outcome, then mark its duration. Choices of damage type are made before rolling; no ability in this revision inspects an individual die to select a second unrelated effect.

A card's full activity time overrides its combat action label. Crafting and using a crafted supply are separate procedures. Do not reduce an hour of work to a Main Action because the action field uses that label for sorting.

Outcome bullets are complete results, not cumulative instructions: apply only the rolled bullet. Where it says “also” or “both benefits,” apply those stated benefits as well. Instant damage happens once; numbered conditions then follow their own resolve-and-decay rules. A duration field never makes attack damage recur.

For an area described as “within N squares,” every selected square must be in range. A connected placed area uses edge-sharing squares. Rectangles extend in a chosen grid direction from a square adjacent to the caster; choose their footprint before rolling. Include allies only where the card targets every creature. Resolve multiple displacements in an order the acting player chooses, using the shared collision rules; unresolved moving-group geometry remains a DA ruling.

Use the character's existing roll for a reaction that modifies that roll. A card which grants Basic Melee directs its recipient to the Basic Melee card; “no separate roll” never makes the granted attack automatic Strong. A player attack still gets one roll and never causes a second player defense roll.

A Boon to defense against forced movement applies to an attack's ordinary defense if that attack can move the defender. It never creates an extra defense against no-roll displacement. Cards that depend on a defense roll do nothing when the normal player-attacker rule supplies no such roll.

VTT records should store action, full time, attribute or delegated roll, targets, range, shape, choices, outcomes, equipment, cost, condition rating, duration anchor, and use limit separately. Track a continuing benefit as one effect with its stated expiry, not a fresh bonus every time the token is selected. Narrative, physical plausibility, willing participation and DA judgments stay visible to the people playing; do not turn them into extra automated saves.

Class signature standard

Agreed: signatures define their class and are slightly more powerful than shared cards at the same tier. Give each choice a useful, recognizable advantage: better action efficiency, reliability, scope, positioning or a distinctive permission. A vivid name alone does not establish that advantage. Compare the whole procedure, including costs, targets and limits, rather than only damage.

Each milestone offers independent choices. Require only class and minimum level; never require an earlier signature. All learned signatures remain available, so review combinations of purchased passives as well as individual cards.

Signature records retain Type: Signature and use Tags for their functional roles; action cost remains a separate field.

Focused Maneuver development

Agreed direction: use Maneuvers for special positioning, setup and support. Keep ordinary movement simple; do not introduce movement-priced ability activations or add variable-cost/conversion cards merely to fill a catalog category. Independent options span all three tiers.

Stability and movement

All pushes, pulls and throws of creatures use @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.5ebfaad0d5ed6813.JournalEntryPage.3292b6a49dcf7236]{Stability}, including additional creatures struck in a collision chain. Distances on cards are before Stability. Other riders still apply when displacement is reduced to 0. Voluntary movement, projectile range, obstacle progress and grapple reduction are not reduced by Stability. Any exception must be explicit on the card.
